title: Wein aa Ramallah
subtitle: Palestinian traditional · Etno orkestar arr. 30-09-26
key: D minor · Maqam Bayati on D
scale: D  E half-flat  F  G  A  Bb  C  (Bayati: the 2nd step is a quarter-tone, E half-flat; guitar chords avoid E)

lines.text: Wein aa Ramallah, wein aa Ramallah,
lines.translation: Where to? To Ramallah! Where to? To Ramallah!
My love, you traveller, where to? To Ramallah!

lines.text: matakhaf min allah, matakhaf min allah,
lines.translation: Don't you fear God? Don't you fear God?
You stole my heart, don't you fear God?

lines.text: Wein aa Ramallah, wein aa Ramallah,
lines.translation: Where to? To Ramallah! Where to? To Ramallah!
My love, you traveller, where to? To Ramallah!

lines.text: dab galby wallah, dab galby wallah,
lines.translation: My heart melted, I swear, my heart melted, I swear,

lines.text: yom ill wadaatak dab galby wallah.
lines.translation: the day I said goodbye to you, my heart melted, I swear.

lines.text: Wain ya habibi, wain ya habibi,
lines.translation: Where, my love? Where, my love?

lines.text: tariknee w raiyeh wain ya habibi,
lines.translation: You leave me and go away, where, my love?

lines.text: hathi w naseeby, hathi w naseeby,
lines.translation: This is my fate, this is my fate,

lines.text: raytak min allah hathi w naseeby.
lines.translation: I saw you as God's gift, this is my fate.

arrangement: Start from silence, count 1 2 3 (heard on the 30-09-26 recording).
Rhythm malfouf all through ("TILILILI ... ritam MAFOUF").
No arrangement flipchart exists for this song; the form follows the three stanzas of the lyric sheet.
notes: No chord board exists for this song: every chord comes from the recording analysis (low-medium confidence).
evidence: Tempo ~129 BPM from the librosa beat tracker on drums+mix; malfouf is a 2/4 feel, so ~65 half-time is the same groove.
Demucs htdemucs stems (other+bass) -> CQT chroma, 0.93 s windows (2 beats at 129 BPM), Viterbi over Dm,Gm,C,A,A7,Bb,F,Cm,Eb.
Chroma path: Dm dominates; Gm blocks of ~5 s at 0:58 and 1:36; A7->Dm cadences at 1:05-1:10 and 1:23. Free-vocabulary best chord mostly Dm7/Gm7.
2:06-2:24: free best E7 / C#m7 (C#, E, G#), an A-major colour; could be an instrumental or the 3rd stanza over A.
basic-pitch MIDI of the 'other' stem: A 1.00, D 0.63, G 0.46, Bb 0.32, F 0.29, C 0.14, E 0.10; low notes D. Consistent with D minor / Bayati with a D-A drone.
DaVinci Resolve Voice Isolation render of the vocal (21.11.2026) used for vocal-activity windows.
uncertain: Title spelled 'Wein a Ramallah' in Pjesme tekstovi.pdf, 'Wein aa Ramallah' in the lines and file names; 'aa' used.
'raytak min allah' translated 'I saw you as God's gift'; the INFO sheet says 'I loved you for God's sake'. Literal: 'I saw you from God'.
Chords are audio-only (no chord flipchart). The line-by-line placement is a best fit of the Dm / Gm / A7 pattern heard; stanza 3 may move to A (see evidence).
